expected_warnings.justification: The fusion overhang is GCGG, which is all G and C. A scarless Golden Gate join takes its 4 bp overhang from the downstream fragment's own first four bases, and this junction falls in a GC rich stretch of the EF1A promoter. The alternatives are to move the junction, which changes which bases end up in the construct, or to insert filler and leave a scar, which defeats the point of using a Type IIS enzyme. An all GC overhang ligates less efficiently, so the correct behaviour is to say so and let the designer decide, which is why Appendix D and section 7.5 check 17 make this a WARN and not a FAIL.

rationale: A BsaI Golden Gate assembly whose downstream fragment begins GCGG. Every other check, including the two overhang failure conditions in checks 15 and 16, passes.

expected_warnings.justification: The amplicon is 60 bp, under the 100 bp floor. Small parts of this size are ordinary: an epitope tag, a linker, a localisation signal, a short terminator. The floor exists because a 60 bp product is hard to tell from primer dimer on a gel and is easy to lose in a cleanup column, which is advice about how to run the reaction rather than a reason not to build the construct. The right answer is to warn and to say what to do about it, which the message does.

rationale: A single 60 bp real fragment amplified by PCR. Every primer check passes; the only warning is the deliberate small size of the part.

expected_warnings.justification: One primer's 3' terminal region fails the composition rule in section 7.5 check 5. The primer ends where the fragment ends, and the fragment boundary is the thing being cloned: moving the primer by two bases to improve the 3' end would amplify a different fragment. A 3' end that is not ideal reduces priming efficiency, which is fixed by raising the annealing stringency or by adding a cycle, not by changing the construct, so the correct severity is WARN.

rationale: A single real 150 bp fragment whose own terminus determines the primer's 3' end. Every other primer and amplicon check passes.

expected_warnings.justification: A primer sits outside the 40 to 60 percent GC window because this part of the CBh promoter record is GC rich, and the primer has to sit at the fragment boundary. The 40 to 60 percent window is a recommendation for typical primers, not a synthesis limit: the much wider 20 to 80 percent window is the one that describes what can actually be made and amplified. Promoters and other regulatory elements are frequently GC rich, so a validator that failed this would reject a large part of real regulatory cloning.

rationale: A single real 150 bp fragment from a GC rich stretch of the CBh record. The one warning is composition that the target sequence dictates.

expected_warnings.justification: A primer carries a run of more than five identical bases because the bGH polyadenylation signal itself contains one. The run is in the part, not in the primer design: amplifying the real bGH polyA means amplifying its homopolymer. Long runs cause polymerase slippage and raise the synthesis error rate, which is a real risk and worth surfacing, but it is a property of the sequence being cloned, so WARN rather than FAIL is right.

rationale: A single 150 bp fragment of the real bGH polyA record. The only warning comes from the part's own homopolymer run.
